PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX rdf:  <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>  # uncomment if you want to filter out rdf:type edges

SELECT DISTINCT ?result ?hop ?via1 ?via2 ?via3 ?via4 ?via5 ?resultLabel
WHERE {
  # Resolve the start node (case-insensitive match on the ID value)
  ?start ?idProp ?idCandidate .
  FILTER( LCASE(STR(?idCandidate)) = LCASE("{{this.nodeID}}") )

  # Hops (1-5)

  # 1 hop
  {
    ?start ?via1 ?result .
    BIND(1 AS ?hop)
  }
  UNION
  # 2 hops
  {
    ?start ?via1 ?mid1 .
    ?mid1  ?via2 ?result .
    BIND(2 AS ?hop)
  }
  UNION
  # 3 hops
  {
    ?start ?via1 ?mid1 .
    ?mid1  ?via2 ?mid2 .
    ?mid2  ?via3 ?result .
    BIND(3 AS ?hop)
  }
  UNION
  # 4 hops
  {
    ?start ?via1 ?mid1 .
    ?mid1  ?via2 ?mid2 .
    ?mid2  ?via3 ?mid3 .
    ?mid3  ?via4 ?result .
    BIND(4 AS ?hop)
  }
  UNION
  # 5 hops
  {
    ?start ?via1 ?mid1 .
    ?mid1  ?via2 ?mid2 .
    ?mid2  ?via3 ?mid3 .
    ?mid3  ?via4 ?mid4 .
    ?mid4  ?via5 ?result .
    BIND(5 AS ?hop)
  }

  ?result a <{{this.targetType}}> .

  # Optional label
  OPTIONAL { ?result rdfs:label ?resultLabel }

  # Optional hygiene (examples)
  # Exclude rdf:type edges from traversal:
  FILTER( COALESCE(?via1, rdfs:label) != rdf:type
        && COALESCE(?via2, rdfs:label) != rdf:type
        && COALESCE(?via3, rdfs:label) != rdf:type
        && COALESCE(?via4, rdfs:label) != rdf:type
        && COALESCE(?via5, rdfs:label) != rdf:type )
}
LIMIT 50

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION assess_data_availability(
    topics TEXT[],
    from_epoch INTEGER,
    to_epoch INTEGER,
    quality_metrics BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    topic_path TEXT,
    data_point_count BIGINT,
    time_coverage_start TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    time_coverage_end TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,
    coverage_percentage NUMERIC(5,2),
    gap_count INTEGER,
    largest_gap_seconds INTEGER,
    avg_interval_seconds NUMERIC,
    quality_score NUMERIC(3,2),
    null_value_percentage NUMERIC(5,2),
    duplicate_count BIGINT
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    WITH     topic_data AS (
        -- Main data extraction using your schema: timestamp, asset_value, topic
        SELECT 
            d.topic,
            d.timestamp,
            d.asset_value
        FROM asset_data d
        WHERE d.topic = ANY(topics)
          AND d.timestamp BETWEEN to_timestamp(from_epoch) AND to_timestamp(to_epoch)
    ),
    
    basic_stats AS (
        SELECT 
            td.topic,
            COUNT(*) as point_count,
            MIN(td.timestamp) as coverage_start,
            MAX(td.timestamp) as coverage_end,
            -- Calculate coverage percentage
            CASE 
                WHEN to_epoch = from_epoch THEN 100.0
                ELSE ROUND(
                    (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (MAX(td.timestamp) - MIN(td.timestamp)))::NUMERIC / 
                     (to_epoch - from_epoch)::NUMERIC) * 100, 2
                )
            END as coverage_pct,
            -- Calculate average interval between data points
            CASE 
                WHEN COUNT(*) > 1 THEN 
                    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (MAX(td.timestamp) - MIN(td.timestamp)))::NUMERIC / (COUNT(*) - 1)
                ELSE NULL
            END as avg_interval
        FROM topic_data td
        GROUP BY td.topic
    ),
    
    gap_analysis AS (
        SELECT 
            td.topic,
            EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (td.timestamp - LAG(td.timestamp) OVER (
                PARTITION BY td.topic ORDER BY td.timestamp
            ))) as gap_seconds
        FROM topic_data td
    ),
    
    gap_stats AS (
        SELECT 
            ga.topic,
            bs.avg_interval,
            -- Count gaps (intervals larger than 2x average)
            COUNT(CASE 
                WHEN ga.gap_seconds > (bs.avg_interval * 2) 
                THEN 1 
            END)::INTEGER as gap_count,
            -- Find largest gap
            MAX(ga.gap_seconds)::INTEGER as largest_gap
        FROM gap_analysis ga
        JOIN basic_stats bs ON ga.topic = bs.topic
        WHERE ga.gap_seconds IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY ga.topic, bs.avg_interval
    ),
    
    quality_analysis AS (
        SELECT 
            td.topic,
            -- Quality score based on data completeness (no quality_flag column available)
            CASE 
                WHEN quality_metrics THEN
                    ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN td.asset_value IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END)::NUMERIC / COUNT(*)::NUMERIC), 2)
                ELSE NULL
            END as quality_score,
            -- Null value percentage
            CASE 
                WHEN quality_metrics THEN
                    ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN td.asset_value IS NULL THEN 1 END)::NUMERIC / COUNT(*)::NUMERIC) * 100, 2)
                ELSE NULL
            END as null_pct,
            -- Duplicate count (same timestamp + asset_value)
            CASE 
                WHEN quality_metrics THEN
                    COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT (td.timestamp, td.asset_value))
                ELSE NULL
            END as duplicate_cnt
        FROM topic_data td
        GROUP BY td.topic
    ),
    
    -- Handle topics with no data
    all_topics AS (
        SELECT unnest(topics) as topic
    )
    
    SELECT 
        at.topic as topic_path,
        COALESCE(bs.point_count, 0) as data_point_count,
        bs.coverage_start as time_coverage_start,
        bs.coverage_end as time_coverage_end,
        COALESCE(bs.coverage_pct, 0.0) as coverage_percentage,
        COALESCE(gs.gap_count, 0) as gap_count,
        gs.largest_gap as largest_gap_seconds,
        bs.avg_interval as avg_interval_seconds,
        qa.quality_score,
        qa.null_pct as null_value_percentage,
        qa.duplicate_cnt as duplicate_count
    FROM all_topics at
    LEFT JOIN basic_stats bs ON at.topic = bs.topic
    LEFT JOIN gap_stats gs ON at.topic = gs.topic
    LEFT JOIN quality_analysis qa ON at.topic = qa.topic
    ORDER BY at.topic;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

WITH columns AS (
  SELECT
    table_name,
    column_name
  FROM information_schema.columns
  WHERE table_schema = 'public'
    AND table_name IN ('Crusher', 'DrumDryer', 'Granulator', 'Mixer', 'Packer')
    AND column_name != '_path'
), paths AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT _path, 'Crusher' AS table_name FROM "public"."Crusher"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT _path, 'DrumDryer' AS table_name FROM "public"."DrumDryer"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT _path, 'Granulator' AS table_name FROM "public"."Granulator"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT _path, 'Mixer' AS table_name FROM "public"."Mixer"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DISTINCT _path, 'Packer' AS table_name FROM "public"."Packer"
)
SELECT
  paths._path || '.' || columns.column_name AS full_path
FROM columns
JOIN paths ON columns.table_name = paths.table_name
ORDER BY full_path;

Data Availability Assessment Tool
Purpose: Quickly assesses data availability and quality for topics within time ranges before executing expensive historical queries.
Parameters:

topics (array, required): List of UNS topic paths to assess
from_epoch (integer, required): Start timestamp
to_epoch (integer, required): End timestamp
quality_metrics (boolean, optional): Include data quality indicators

Returns: Per-topic summary of data point counts, time coverage, gaps, and quality indicators.

pipelines.name: UnsHistoricalDataRetrievalTool
pipelines.description:
Historical UNS Data Retrieval Tool
Purpose: Retrieves comprehensive historical data from a specified Unified Namespace (UNS) topic within a defined time range.
Input Parameters:

topic (string, required): The Unified Namespace topic path to query (e.g., "enterprise/site/area/line/device/tag")
from_epoch (integer, required): Start timestamp in Unix epoch time (seconds since January 1, 1970 UTC)
to_epoch (integer, required): End timestamp in Unix epoch time (seconds since January 1, 1970 UTC)

Returns: Complete historical dataset for the specified UNS topic, including all data points, values, timestamps, and metadata that occurred within the specified time window. The response preserves the original data structure and chronological ordering.
Use Cases:

Industrial analytics and trend analysis
Compliance reporting and audit trails
Performance optimization studies
Root cause analysis of operational events
Data migration and archival operations

Notes:

Time range is inclusive of both start and end timestamps
Large time ranges may result in substantial data volumes
Supports standard UNS hierarchical topic structures
Maintains full data fidelity without sampling or aggregation

This tool enables comprehensive historical data extraction from UNS-compliant systems for analysis, reporting, and operational intelligence purposes.

pipelines.name: UnsOntologyFilterOnKeyword
pipelines.description:
Use this tool to find specific nodes or classes in the graph-database (GraphDB) based on the input parameter string.
Input Parameter:
keyword (full string, required): The string that will search rdfs:label and rdfs:comment and find the associated nodes (e.g., "batch")
Output:
Will return a json formated output with three output parameters: {?nodeIRI, ?predicateType, ?text}

The outputs include the node IRI (location), the type of predicate containing the string, and the text in string format that contained the keyword.

pipelines.name: UnsOntologyReturnMetadata
pipelines.description:
Use this tool to read metadata about a specific node in the graph-database (GraphDB).
Input Parameter:
keyword (full IRI, required): The IRI will be used to locate the specific node in the graph-database and find the associated properties (e.g., "http://continuaps.com/data#VIALFILLER_DEMO").
***If only the node name without the partial IRI is provided the query will return None***
Output:
Will return a json formated output with two output parameters: {?property, ?value}

The output includes the predicate describing the property and then the value of the of the property.

pipelines.name: UnsOntologyReturnNodeByFilteringTimestamps
pipelines.description:
Use this tool to find any nodes of the inputted type and then return results that are within a window based on the provided start and end timestamps. Only use this tool if dates are provided in the prompt. 
Input Parameters:
There are three input parameters.
nodeType (full IRI, required): The IRI will be used to locate the node of a specific type in the graph-database (e.g., "http://purl.org/isa88#Unit")
startDate (ISO 8601 format, required): This timestamp represents the start of the window (e.g. "2025-05-26T09:00:00Z")
endDate (ISO 8601 format, required): This timestamp represents the end of the window (e.g. "2025-05-26T09:00:00Z")
Output:
Will return a json formated output with four output parameters: {?entity, ?class, ?start, ?end}

Where ?entity and ?class will be the node name and the node class. ?start and ?end are the timestamps associated with ?entity

pipelines.name: UnsOntologyReturnPointedSearchRangeFiveHops
pipelines.description:
Use this tool to find nodes of the target type within five hops starting from a specific node that is defined by the user specified ID.
Input Parameters:
There are two input parameters.
nodeID (string, required): This string will be used to locate the node that has this specific ID in the graph-database (e.g., "BATCH20250525-A")
targetType (full IRI, required): This represents the type we are searching for (***Will have association with the class attached to the nodeID***). (e.g. "http://purl.org/isa88#Unit")
Output:
Will return a json formated output with eight output parameters: {?result, ?hop, ?via1, ?via2, ?via3, ?via4, ?via5, ?resultLabel}

?result will be the name of the node found in "x" number of hops
?hop will be the number of hops required to reach ?result
?via1 will be the predicate for the first hop to reach ?result
?via2 will be the predicate for the second hop to reach ?result
?via3 will be the predicate for the third hop to reach ?result
?via4 will be the predicate for the fourth hop to reach ?result
?via5 will be the predicate for the fifth hop to reach ?result
?resultLabel will be the label associated with ?result if available
